new_task_1.title: Use resolved package names in MSBuildDeps component imports
new_task_1.description: Conan 2.15.0 fixes `MSBuildDeps` so generated component dependency imports use the resolved dependency package name instead of the original requested name. This keeps generated `.props` references correct when `replace_requires` remaps a dependency to a different package name.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `MSBuildDeps` generates component dependency imports using the actual resolved dependency package name, so MSBuild generator output remains valid when dependency replacement changes the package name seen in the graph.

expectation.grounded: When `MSBuildDeps` processes a component requirement that points to a component in another package, it should look up the resolved dependency entry from `pkg_deps` and derive the emitted public dependency name from `required.ref.name`. If the requirement targets that package's root component, the emitted dependency name should be the resolved package name alone; if it targets a named component, the emitted dependency should use the resolved package name plus the component suffix. Dependencies that were skipped and are absent from `pkg_deps` should continue to be omitted.
expectation.conceptual: Generated MSBuild props files should follow the dependency graph that Conan actually resolved, not the package name that originally appeared in the recipe before replacement rules were applied.

constraints.grounded: This fix applies only to cross-package component requirements in `MSBuildDeps`. Same-package component references should keep using the current package naming path, and transitive dependencies that are not present in `pkg_deps` should still not generate import entries. The component portion of the dependency name should remain unchanged apart from swapping in the resolved package name.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be narrowly scoped to correcting emitted dependency identifiers for replaced or aliased package names without altering normal dependency skipping or same-package component behavior.

behavior: Cross-package component dependencies generated by `MSBuildDeps` now use the resolved dependency package name from the graph.
When a dependency replacement changes a package name, generated `.props` imports point to the replacement package's files instead of the original package name.
When the dependency refers to a specific component, the generated dependency identifier keeps that component name while swapping in the resolved package name.
When a transitive dependency was skipped and is not present in `pkg_deps`, `MSBuildDeps` continues to omit that public dependency entry.
acceptance_criteria: When `replace_requires` remaps a dependency package to a different package name and `MSBuildDeps` generates props files, imports should reference the replacement package name rather than the original requested package name.
When a generated MSBuild dependency import targets the replacement package's root target, the emitted import should use the resolved package name without an incorrect legacy package prefix.
When a generated MSBuild dependency import targets a named component of the replacement package, the emitted import should use the resolved package name together with the expected component suffix.
When a transitive cross-package dependency is absent because it was skipped, `MSBuildDeps` should continue generating without adding a dangling public dependency import.
When no package-name replacement occurs, cross-package component dependency generation should continue to produce the same dependency structure as before.
